matches.title: Torino vs Sassuolo
matches.description: Watch Torino vs Sassuolo highlights and goals from Serie A on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 8, 2026. On 2026-05-08, the Stadio Olimpico Grande Torino played host to a captivating Serie A clash between Torino and Sassuolo . Both teams entered the pitch with clear tactical objectives, setting the stage for a contest defined by discipline and sudden shifts in momentum. Defensive Resilience in the Opening Period The first half was a testament to organized defending, with both sides struggling to break the deadlock despite several set-piece opportunities. Sassuolo came closest to an opener in the 14th minute when Tarik Muharemovic saw his goal-bound effort hacked off the line by the Torino defense following an Armand Lauriente corner. While the hosts controlled periods of possession, their delivery from wide areas often failed to find a teammate, leaving the 18,000 fans in attendance waiting for the first breakthrough at the interval. A Dramatic Turnaround in the Second Half The game exploded into life shortly after the restart. In the 51st minute, Sassuolo took the lead as Kristian Thorstvedt found space to tap home a Luca Lipani assist with his left foot. This goal prompted Torino into a double substitution, bringing on Duvan Zapata and Marcus Holmgren Pedersen to sharpen their attack. The tactical shift paid dividends in the 66th minute when Giovanni Simeone rose highest to head home an equalizer following a cross from Enzo Ebosse . The momentum had firmly shifted, and just four minutes later, Torino struck again. Nikola Vlasic played a short corner to set up Marcus Holmgren Pedersen , who powered a header into the back of the net to make it 2-1. Despite late pressure from the visitors—including a missed header from Ulisses Garcia in stoppage time—and a flurry of yellow cards for Niels Nkounkou and Gvidas Gineitis , the home side held firm to secure a hard-fought victory.

The Turin derby delivered the intensity and historical rivalry expected as Torino hosted Juventus on May 24, 2026. Throughout this Serie A encounter, the momentum swung back and forth, creating a high-stakes atmosphere that kept fans on the edge of their seats. Early Momentum and Clinical Finishing Juventus set the tone early in the match, finding the breakthrough in the 24th minute when Dusan Vlahovic struck with his left foot, set up by a clever assist from Khephren Thuram-Ulien and a key pass from Pierre Kalulu . Despite Torino attempting to find a rhythm through various corner kicks and build-up play, the visitors remained compact. Following the interval, Juventus pushed to extend their lead, and they succeeded in the 54th minute when Dusan Vlahovic netted his second of the game, finishing a well-constructed move assisted by Chico Conceição . The Fightback and Final Drama Trailing by two, the hosts refused to concede defeat and ramped up their tactical aggression. Cesare Casadei sparked hope in the 60th minute, leaping to head home a dangerous delivery from Rafael Obrador . The game turned into a frantic battle as both managers introduced fresh legs to influence the outcome. The pressure finally told in the 84th minute, as Che Adams reacted quickest to a loose ball, slotting home to level the score. Despite a series of late tactical changes and mounting tension in stoppage time, both sides had to settle for a share of the spoils in a hard-fought Serie A clash.

matches.title: Cagliari vs Torino

Cagliari hosted an intense Serie A fixture on May 17, 2026, where the tactical battle between the two sides unfolded into a captivating display of professional football. The match provided a sharp contrast of momentum shifts that kept the atmosphere electric throughout the afternoon. First-half fireworks The game roared into life in the 38th minute when Rafael Obrador fired a stunning long-range effort to put Torino in front. The lead was short-lived, however, as Sebastiano Esposito leveled the score just one minute later, thanks to a clever assist from Matteo Prati . Just as the first half appeared set to end on even terms, Yerry Mina rose highest in the 45+2 minute to head home, handing Cagliari the lead heading into the break. A dramatic conclusion The second half saw Torino push aggressively for an equalizer, bringing on fresh legs like Andrea Belotti to sharpen their attack. As the game entered its closing stages, tempers flared, resulting in yellow cards for Guillermo Maripan and Paul Mendy due to a scuffle in the 82nd minute. The drama reached its zenith in the seventh minute of injury time, when the referee halted play to review a potential penalty for Torino via VAR . Following the review, the original decision not to award the spot-kick stood, allowing Cagliari to hold onto their advantage until the final whistle.
